levels.cheer: The gymnastics team lines up in 4 rows. There are 6 gymnasts in every row. 🤸
levels.question: How many gymnasts altogether?
hints: 4 rows of 6 means 4 sixes added up.

levels.name: Dance Lines
levels.cheer: 24 dancers need to split into 4 equal lines for the routine. 💃
levels.question: How many dancers in each line?

levels.name: Song Practice

hints: 7 × 8 is the same as 7 × 4 twice: 28 and 28.

verses.text: I can do all things through Christ, who strengthens me.
Let us not be weary in doing good…
For God didn’t give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.

teach.heading: Groups that match
teach.body: Multiplying is just adding the same number again and again. If 3 dancers hold 4 ribbons each, that is 3 groups of 4.

teach.heading: The groups must be equal
teach.body: This only works if every group is the same size. If one dancer has 4 ribbons and one has 7, you cannot multiply. You have to add.

teach.heading: Say it out loud
teach.body: Read 3 x 4 as "3 groups of 4." It helps you picture it. Then count them up.

practice.question: How many song sheets?
practice.explain: 5 groups of 2. Count: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.

practice.prompt: One dancer has 3 bows. One has 6 bows. One has 1 bow.
practice.question: Can you multiply to find the total?
choices: No, the groups are not equal
practice.correct: No, the groups are not equal
practice.explain: The groups are different sizes. You must add: 3 + 6 + 1 = 10.

practice.question: What is the short way to write it?
practice.explain: There are five 4s. That is 5 groups of 4, or 5 x 4 = 20.

practice.prompt: A coach says "6 x 3" out loud.
practice.question: What does that mean?
practice.explain: The x means groups of. 6 groups of 3 is 18.

reinforce.prompt: One box has 5 ribbons. One box has 9 ribbons.
reinforce.question: Can you multiply?

lessons.title: Skip counting
lessons.subtitle: A fast way to count groups.

teach.heading: Jump, do not crawl
teach.body: You do not have to count every single thing. You can jump. To count groups of 5, jump by 5s.

teach.heading: It is the same as multiplying
teach.body: Every jump is one more group. Jump 4 times by 5 and you have done 4 x 5.

teach.heading: The easy ones
teach.body: Twos, fives and tens are the easiest jumps. Learn those first and a lot of maths gets faster.

practice.prompt: Start at 0 and jump by 5, four times.
practice.question: Where do you land?
What comes next?
practice.explain: You are jumping by 2 each time. 8 + 2 = 10.

practice.question: What comes next?
practice.explain: Jumping by 10. 30 + 10 = 40.

lessons.title: Rows and columns
lessons.subtitle: Lining things up makes it easy.

teach.heading: Lines that match
teach.body: When things line up in rows, every row is a group. Count one row. Then count how many rows.

teach.heading: It works both ways
teach.body: You can count rows or count columns. You get the same answer. 4 x 6 and 6 x 4 both make 24.

teach.heading: That is a handy trick
teach.body: If one way is hard, flip it. 2 x 9 might feel tricky. 9 x 2 is just double 9.
teach.example: 2 x 9  is the same as  9 x 2  =  18

practice.prompt: The squad lines up in 3 rows. Each row has 6 girls.
practice.question: How many girls?

practice.prompt: Someone says 5 x 3 and 3 x 5 give different answers.
practice.question: Are they right?
practice.explain: Flipping the order never changes the answer.

practice.question: How many chairs?
practice.explain: 2 rows of 8. Or flip it: 8 + 8 = 16.

practice.prompt: You find 7 x 2 hard, but you know doubles well.
practice.question: What is the easier way?
choices: Flip it to 2 x 7 and double 7
practice.correct: Flip it to 2 x 7 and double 7
practice.explain: Double 7 is 14. Flipping is allowed and it is faster.

reinforce.prompt: Is 6 x 2 the same as 2 x 6?
reinforce.question: Pick one.
reinforce.explain: Order does not matter when you multiply.

reinforce.question: What is the easy way?
reinforce.explain: Double 9 is 18. Same answer, less work.

teach.heading: Fair shares
teach.body: Dividing means sharing something out so everyone gets the same. If 12 ribbons go to 3 girls, each one gets 4.

teach.heading: Everyone gets the same
teach.body: It is only dividing if the shares are equal. One girl cannot get 6 while another gets 2.

teach.heading: Two ways to ask it
teach.body: 12 ÷ 3 can mean share into 3 groups. Or it can mean how many groups of 3 fit in 12. Both give 4.

practice.prompt: 20 medals are shared by 4 gymnasts. Everyone gets the same.
practice.question: How many each?
practice.explain: 20 shared 4 ways. 4 x 5 = 20, so each gets 5.

practice.prompt: 18 girls need to make lines of 6.
practice.question: How many lines?
practice.explain: How many 6s fit in 18? 6, 12, 18. That is 3 lines.

practice.prompt: 10 sweets. One girl takes 7. The other gets 3.
practice.question: Did they divide them?
choices: No, the shares are not equal
practice.correct: No, the shares are not equal
practice.explain: Dividing means equal shares. 5 and 5 would be dividing.

practice.question: How many each?
practice.explain: 5 x 3 = 15, so each dancer gets 3.

reinforce.prompt: 9 stickers. One girl gets 8, one gets 1.
reinforce.question: Is that dividing?

teach.heading: One undoes the other
teach.body: Multiplying makes groups. Dividing takes them apart. They are opposites, like adding and taking away.

teach.heading: Three facts, one family
teach.body: If you know one, you know the others. 3, 4 and 12 belong together. You can write them four ways.

teach.heading: Use it to check
teach.body: Finished a divide? Multiply it back. If you land where you started, you got it right.

practice.question: So what is 30 ÷ 5?
practice.explain: Dividing undoes multiplying. The 6 comes straight back.

practice.prompt: You work out 24 ÷ 4 = 6 and want to check it.
practice.question: What should you do?
choices: Multiply 4 x 6 and see if you get 24
practice.correct: Multiply 4 x 6 and see if you get 24
practice.explain: 4 x 6 = 24. It checks out.

practice.prompt: The numbers 2, 8 and 16 are a family.
practice.question: Which one is NOT in that family?
practice.explain: 3 and 5 are not part of this family. The other three are.

practice.question: What is 21 ÷ 7?
practice.explain: Same family. Dividing by 7 gives back the 3.

reinforce.question: How do you check it?
reinforce.explain: It is 18, so you were right.
